schedule.aiSummary: Day 1 in Delhi: Explore Qutub Minar, Red Fort with curated visits and local culture.

activities.name: Qutub Minar
activities.description: A 72.5-meter fluted red sandstone minaret erected in 1192 by Qutb-ud-din Aibak. A UNESCO World Heritage site surrounded by medieval architectural monuments including the Iron Pillar of Delhi.
activities.aiReason: Verified canonical history highlighting the heritage of Delhi.
aiTips: Book tickets in advance during peak visiting hours
Wear comfortable footwear and carry water

activities.name: Red Fort
activities.description: Historic fortified palace complex constructed in 1639 by Emperor Shah Jahan. Built of red sandstone, it represents the zenith of Mughal creativity and has served as a primary national landmark of India.
activities.aiReason: Verified canonical history highlighting the heritage of Delhi.
aiTips: Book tickets in advance during peak visiting hours
Wear comfortable footwear and carry water

schedule.aiSummary: Day 2 in Delhi: Explore Humayun's Tomb, Lodhi Garden with curated visits and local culture.

activities.name: Humayun's Tomb
activities.description: The tomb of the Mughal Emperor Humayun, commissioned by his first wife Empress Bega Begum in 1558. It was the first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent, inspiring the architectural design of the Taj Mahal.
activities.aiReason: Verified canonical architecture highlighting the heritage of Delhi.
aiTips: Book tickets in advance during peak visiting hours
Wear comfortable footwear and carry water

activities.name: Lodhi Garden
activities.description: A city park situated in New Delhi covering 90 acres. Contains the architectural tombs of Mohammed Shah and Sikandar Lodi, surrounded by landscaped lawns, manicured trees, and serene walking tracks.
activities.aiReason: Verified canonical nature highlighting the heritage of Delhi.
aiTips: Book tickets in advance during peak visiting hours
Wear comfortable footwear and carry water
